Erratas

The Errata register only exists for published versions that have received corrections. Try one of:.

← Back to current Erratas

The authoritative register of corrections to published documentation against — the TPP Standards, LFI Integration Guide, and OpenAPI specifications. Each entry records what was corrected, why the change was required, and the effective date.

Erratas > Find a correction

Narrow by audience, functional area, or section. Add a keyword to refine further. Click a section chip on a result row to open the page the correction applies to.

Try removing a filter or clearing the keyword. The pill counts above show how many sections each filter would surface on its own.

Erratas > How this register works

The Errata register is bound by the policies that control how published content evolves. Once a version is published, its existing content MUST NOT be changed without an associated Errata record.

Erratas > How this register works > Changes to Published Documentation

How published content may change after release — what requires an Errata, what does not, and how corrections are communicated.

Erratas > How this register works > Version Management

How versions are numbered, when errata releases are cut, and how the relationship between Standards, API Hub, and Ozone Connect versions is maintained.

- Each entry has a unique identifier in the form <version>-errata<n> — for example, v2.1-errata2.
- Each entry states the affected document(s) and section(s), what changed, why the change was required, and the effective date.
- Existing published content MUST NOT be changed without an associated Errata record.
- Pre-publication content (for example -rc, -rc-final ) can be updated without an Errata.
